title: The tragic tale of old macdonald`s farm a personnel saga
summary: A short satirical piece that parodies the nursery rhyme "Old MacDonald Had a Farm" by recasting the farm as a workplace governed by bureaucratic personnel and procurement rules. A retired university Personnel Officer buys a farm, labels his animals with formal Job Titles and Job Descriptions, and assigns his wife the title of Procurement Officer. When a neighbour tries to buy a milk cow, the narrative piles up absurd obstacles: reclassification requests in quintuplicate, sole-source justifications, three-bid requirements, and rules forbidding discrimination by breed or age. The humour lies in the mock-serious officialese, the EIEIO acronyms, and the escalating logic that turns simple farming into paperwork. The story ends with the protagonist giving up on farm life to lead a bureaucratic agency of his own. It is a short comic piece about institutional red tape, and it is the sort of thing that circulated as an office-humour parody rather than a full novel.
